title: Riot Games World Championship — Shanghai
tagline: Celebrating ten years of League of Legends Esports with the fans who built it — mid-pandemic.

body: The 10th anniversary of the World Championship was Riot's moment to celebrate a decade of fandom — and it landed in the middle of a pandemic, in China. We faced strict limits on how many people could be on stage, creative partners unable to legally enter the country and music performers unable to travel, among many other challenges.

The show still had to deliver on three fronts: K/DA's return to the main stage in full AR, a tribute to ten years of League of Legends Esports, and a spotlight on the two teams competing for the title.

Riot wanted the biggest celebration in company history — a thank-you to the fans as much as a show. As Creative Director, I led a diverse team of external agencies, stage designers, lighting designers and choreographers to craft an authentic tribute to the tournament's legacy, at the first live event back from the pandemic.

We adapted the vision for months as restrictions shifted, holding onto its core pillars, and delivered a 15-minute experience: a 30-foot-tall set, choreography fused with content, striking lighting and stadium-scale AR that brought League's characters and music to fans around the world.
led: Led external agencies and design teams
Kept the anniversary vision intact through pandemic constraints
Delivered a 15-minute AR celebration of ten years of fandom

impact.note: The ceremony earned Riot Games its third Emmy Award, reached 100M+ viewers and drew acclaim across social — a decade of fandom celebrated at global scale.
